parameters.query: =SELECT COALESCE((SELECT status FROM agent.guide_onboarding_state WHERE section_key = 'household'), 'unknown') AS household_status, COALESCE((SELECT string_agg(format('- %s %s (person_id %s; role %s; birth date %s%s)', pp->>'first_name', pp->>'last_name', pp->>'person_id', pp->>'role', CASE WHEN NULLIF(pp->>'birth_date', '') IS NULL THEN 'missing' ELSE 'stored' END, COALESCE('; also stored: ' || (SELECT string_agg(k, ', ' ORDER BY k) FROM jsonb_object_keys(pp) AS k WHERE k NOT IN ('person_id','first_name','last_name','role','birth_date','as_of','telegram_user_id','aliases')), '')), E'\n' ORDER BY x.ord) FROM agent.core_contexts c, jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(c.metadata->'facts'->'persons', '[]'::jsonb)) WITH ORDINALITY AS x(pp, ord) WHERE c.name = 'family'), '') AS persons;

={{ $('Load Agent Context').item.json.system_prompt + ($('Household status read').item.json.household_status ? ('

## Household so far (from the installation and earlier onboarding - authoritative)
' + ($('Household status read').item.json.persons ? ($('Household status read').item.json.persons + '
Do NOT ask again for the name or birth date of anyone listed here - confirm briefly instead (e.g. Dich kenne ich schon aus der Installation). Ask only for what is still missing (e.g. partner, children, employment).') : 'No household members stored yet.') + '

parameters.toolDescription: Run read-only SELECT queries (role core_ro: schemas `agent` + `core`, plus the schema of every ACTIVE package). Use it to check which package areas still need onboarding (SELECT core.fn_onboarding_pending_packages()) and to look up details before capturing (dedup). The household onboarding status and the stored household members are already in your system prompt (Household so far). Views are narrow: SELECT * if unsure of columns. On a query error you receive it back - correct and retry. No write access.
parameters.query: ={{ ($fromAI('query', 'A read-only PostgreSQL SELECT statement', 'string') || '').trim() || "SELECT false AS ok, 'The query argument is missing - call postgres_select again with one read-only SELECT statement in query.' AS error" }}

parameters.toolDescription: Fetch the full content of a lazy context document by name (see manifest in your system prompt). Load `family` for the full household facts and prose (the member list is already in your prompt); load `capabilities_catalog` for the feature overview incl. the section of functions that can still be added on the server.

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ name: $fromAI('context_name', 'Name of the lazy context document to load (e.g. family, capabilities_catalog)', 'string') }) }}

parameters.name: tool_set_household_facts
parameters.description: SECTION 0 (household) — capture household members and facts into the family context. Pass persons as a JSON ARRAY string and household as a JSON OBJECT string. A NEW person: omit person_id (the system assigns it) and pass first_name AND last_name (always both), birth_date (exact YYYY-MM-DD), role (owner|partner|child), and employment/insurance facts if known (free text stored verbatim in the words the user used, never translated). language = the code of the language for the bot fixed messages, ONLY one of de|en|ko and ONLY if the user states it - do not ask for it (after a new person is saved the owner gets a language button card automatically). Persons already listed in Household so far exist: to add facts to them, pass ONLY their person_id from that list + the new keys (never invent a person_id; the internal id is never shown to the user). Play back values you assembled over several turns before calling; if the user just gave the values with an explicit save instruction, call directly - the tool shows a short button confirmation and merges atomically (ok:false with a reason = rejected, fix and ask).

value.persons: ={{ $fromAI('persons', 'JSON array string of person objects: new person {first_name, last_name, birth_date, role, ...} without person_id; existing person {person_id, ...new keys}', 'string', '') }}
value.household: ={{ $fromAI('household', 'JSON object string of household-level facts (e.g. {"joint_finances": true})', 'string', '') }}
value.context_name: ={{ $fromAI('context_name', 'family (default); or a package household profile (finance_profile) only if that package is active per installed_packages', 'string', 'family') }}
value.content: ={{ $fromAI('content', 'Optional prose body to replace the context document text', 'string', '') }}

parameters.name: tool_set_onboarding_section
parameters.description: Mark the household onboarding section done. Call AFTER you finished (or the user chose to skip) the household. section_key is ALWAYS "household" (the sections of installed packages belong to those packages agents, which mark their own). status = completed (captured) or skipped (user consciously declined - legitimate, recorded) or unknown (reset). Returns onboarding_complete = whether the core (household) part is now resolved.

parameters.name: tool_invite_household_member
parameters.description: Issue a member invitation (OWNER ONLY). When the household owner wants an EXISTING family member to use the bot from their own Telegram ("invite my daughter Lisa", "lade meine Tochter ein", "Partner einladen"), call this with the person name. Returns a one-time deep link the owner shares out-of-band; the member redeems it and the owner confirms by button before access becomes active. NOT for capturing NEW people (that is onboarding via tool_set_household_facts), and the tool itself rejects non-owner callers.

value.person_name: ={{ $fromAI('person_name', 'Name of the existing household member to invite (first name or full name as stored in the family facts)', 'string') }}

parameters.content:
## DB-Automatik
**agent.guide — Help + Household-Onboarding (Sub-Workflow)**

Eingang: task, chat_id, call_depth (vom Orchestrator als Tool gerufen). Pipeline: Depth gate -> Load Config -> System-Prompt+Manifest (agent.tool_load_context, agent_name=guide; enthält den statischen Context installed_packages = welche Pakete aktiv/aus/nicht installiert sind) -> Household status read (core_ro: family-Personen mit Rolle + Geburtsdatum vorhanden ja/nein + Haushalts-Status; Install-UX-Phase 6: der bei der Installation angelegte Owner wird nicht erneut nach Name/Geburtsdatum gefragt) -> Build Agent Input (hängt Household so far an) -> Guide Agent. WS-B3 (O3): der Guide onboardet NUR den Haushalt (Section household) -> tool_set_household_facts (HITL) + tool_set_onboarding_section(household, Tri-State, kein Gate). Die Paket-Onboarding-Sektionen sind paket-besessen und werden vom provides.onboarding-Agenten des jeweiligen Pakets selbst erfasst (Self-Onboarding + eigene Staging-Pipeline + <pkg>.onboarding_state) -> der Guide bindet keine Paket-Staging-/Vision-Tools und verweist für Paket-Bereiche auf /onboarding bzw. den zuständigen Paket-Agenten (nur wenn das Paket laut installed_packages aktiv ist; sonst nennt er den Server-Befehl lifeagents package install). Reads: postgres_select (core_ro) + load_context (context_ro, family/capabilities_catalog). Fachfragen der Pakete gehen über den Orchestrator an deren Agenten; Trigger -> agent.monitor.

## DB-Automatik
**Modellwahl (Config-gesteuert)**

Gemeinsamer Builder New-ModelSelectorBundle: je Claude-Modell ein Node (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus), Selector liest core.config model.guide. Default claude-sonnet-latest, Denk-Tiefe medium (Onboarding ist tool-lastig -> zuverlässiges Function-Calling). Wechsel: lifeagents config set model guide <key>, kein Build.
